headline: A tough day across the board — PLS slid 4%, GXAI dropped 2.8%, and US tech stumbled on earnings jitters last night, while Iran tensions and US midterm drama dominate global headlines.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara fell 4% today, continuing its brutal run — it's now down over 60% on your total investment. No specific news catalyst today, but lithium sentiment remains weak with global EV demand forecasts being revised down. This is a structural story that hasn't turned yet.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: The AI ETF dropped 2.8% today, dragged down by weakness in US tech names overnight — Google and Microsoft both fell on their earnings results last night. The broader AI trade has been choppy this week.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two slipped 1.67% last night in the US session. No major negative news — GTA 6 Vice City trademark filings are actually a positive sign ahead of launch, and a viral 'watermark leak' was debunked by insiders. The dip looks like general market weakness rather than anything company-specific.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft fell 1.55% last night despite reporting Q1 FY27 earnings. The market reaction appears mixed — analysts noted a 'growing divide' in the Magnificent 7 AI trade, with some investors questioning whether Microsoft's cloud AI investments are translating to earnings growth fast enough. Still up 17.8% on your total position.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Alphabet sank 1.45% last night after Q3 results showed $127.6B in revenue but negative free cash flow and a -12.6% FCF drop. The stock dragged the Nasdaq lower. One analyst piece called it 'the 30% earnings miss that wasn't' — suggesting the headline miss was overstated, but the market sold it anyway.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE slipped 1.16% today, likely reflecting global risk-off sentiment with US-Iran tensions pushing up oil and weighing on emerging market stocks. Nothing structural — just the mood of the market.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS eased 0.69% today, tracking last night's weak US session (Nasdaq fell 2.86%, S&P fell 1.82%). Despite today's dip, you're still up 3.4% overall on this position — it continues to do its job as broad US market exposure.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG barely moved today, down just 0.25%. As a diversified multi-asset ETF it's cushioned from single-sector moves. Its slight dip mirrors the mild softness in global markets today.

movers.name: DHHF
movers.note: DHHF was essentially flat, down 0.22%. Nothing to report — this broad global ETF is just ticking along with the general market softness. Virtually no change from yesterday's close.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Hold, but know why you own it
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals dropped another 4% today and is now down over 60% on your investment. The lithium market remains structurally weak with no clear near-term recovery catalyst. That said, if you bought this as a long-term bet on the EV transition, that thesis is still intact — it's just taking much longer than the market expected. Selling now locks in a real loss. Hold unless your investment thesis has genuinely changed.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI ETF taking heat from earnings misses
watch_today.detail: The Global X AI ETF fell 2.8% today, largely because Google and Microsoft both had disappointing earnings reactions last night in the US. You're down 15% overall on this position. The long-term AI growth story is still very real, but short-term volatility will be driven by whether big tech can prove its AI spending is paying off in earnings. No reason to sell — just be prepared for more chop.

watch_today.title: GOOG — Earnings drove the drop, long-term case intact
watch_today.detail: Alphabet fell 1.45% last night after Q3 results showed negative free cash flow for the quarter, down 12.6%. The market sold it hard, dragging the Nasdaq down with it. One analyst framed the miss as overstated. You're down 9.5% overall on a small position. The long-term Google AI and cloud story hasn't broken — this looks like market overreaction to a messy quarter. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: MSFT — Earnings out, cloud AI still the story
watch_today.detail: Microsoft reported Q1 FY27 results last night and dropped 1.55%. Analysts are debating whether Azure (their cloud business) AI revenue is growing fast enough to justify the heavy spending. You're still up nearly 18% on your total position — this is a long-term hold with strong fundamentals. Don't let one earnings night shake you.

watch_today.title: Oil spiking — watch for flow-on inflation effects
watch_today.detail: Crude oil (WTI) jumped 2% last night to US$104 a barrel, driven by escalating US-Iran tensions in the Strait of Hormuz. Ship attacks in October were the highest since the war began. Higher oil means higher petrol prices and could keep inflation sticky — which matters for the RBA rate decision next week.

watch_today.title: RBA rate decision coming — could hit your mortgage and markets
watch_today.detail: The RBA meets next week and Westpac is now tipping a rate hike after hotter-than-expected CPI data. PM Albanese publicly called rate hikes a 'blunt instrument', distancing Labor from the RBA. If the RBA hikes, expect pressure on ASX property and consumer stocks, and potentially a stronger Aussie dollar. Watch this closely.

world.summary: US midterm tensions dominate global news with a court ordering Trump's team to stop threatening election officials. Iran-US conflict is escalating, hitting oil prices. Pope Leo XIV made history voting in a US election. Gulf states are rethinking their entire defence strategy.

stories.title: Judge orders Trump administration to stop threatening election officials ahead of midterms
stories.why_it_matters: A US federal judge has issued an order telling the Trump administration to immediately stop threatening election officials with criminal prosecution ahead of the midterm elections. The order is a significant legal check on executive power — election officials in several states had reportedly been warned they could face charges related to how they count or certify votes. With midterms days away, the ruling is aimed at protecting the integrity of the vote count.

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV becomes first pope in history to vote in a US election
stories.why_it_matters: Pope Leo XIV — the first American-born pope — has cast a vote in the US midterm election, making him the first pope in history to vote in a US general election. As an American citizen, he is legally entitled to vote and chose to exercise that right, which is being seen as both a personal statement and a historic moment. His involvement adds an extraordinary dimension to an already highly charged political event.

stories.title: Iran-US tensions escalate: ship attacks at record high, supreme leader warns of 'unrestricted response'
stories.why_it_matters: Attacks on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz — a critical global oil chokepoint — hit their highest level in October since the US-Iran conflict began. Iran's supreme leader has publicly warned that any fresh US military strikes will trigger a 'geographically unrestricted response', raising the stakes significantly. This is already pushing oil prices above US$104 a barrel, which flows through to higher petrol prices and inflation everywhere, including Australia.

stories.title: Gulf states told to rethink trillion-dollar defence strategy in light of US-Iran war
stories.why_it_matters: A major new report says Gulf states like Saudi Arabia and the UAE need to fundamentally rethink how they spend their trillion-dollar defence budgets, given that the US-Iran conflict has exposed major gaps in regional security architecture. The report comes as Iran braces for possible new strikes while diplomatic talks continue in the background. For Australia, the Middle East instability matters through oil prices, global trade routes, and the risk of wider conflict.

stories.title: Top US law firms that backed down to Trump now sidelined from midterm legal battles
stories.why_it_matters: Several of America's biggest law firms — which earlier struck deals with the Trump administration to avoid being targeted — are now sitting out the midterm election legal battles, leaving voter protection and election integrity work to smaller firms. Critics say the big firms capitulated to political pressure, and now can't be seen to challenge the administration they appeased. It's a window into how the rule of law is being tested ahead of a pivotal US election.

markets.summary: The ASX held up reasonably well today, edging up 0.18%, but last night's US session was ugly — the Nasdaq fell nearly 3% and the S&P dropped 1.82% on disappointing tech earnings. Oil surged on Iran tensions. Gold pulled back sharply. The Aussie dollar is steady.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: The local market held its ground today, up 0.18% — a modest positive session.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's US session saw the S&P fall 1.82%, weighed down by tech earnings disappointments from Google and Microsoft.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: The Nasdaq was hit harder, falling 2.86% last night — Alphabet's earnings dragged the index lower.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil jumped 2% on escalating US-Iran tensions and record ship attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. Watch for petrol price rises.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold had a rough night, falling 3.3% — possibly as traders sold safe-haven assets to cover losses elsewhere.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar nudged slightly higher, helped by bets the RBA could hike rates after hotter-than-expected CPI data this week.

politics.summary: The RBA is in the spotlight ahead of next week's rate decision, with Westpac tipping a hike after hot inflation data. Albanese publicly distanced himself from the RBA. Victoria's budget is in serious trouble, and there are calls to slash the public service to restore a federal surplus.

stories.title: Westpac tips RBA rate hike next week after hot CPI data
stories.why_it_matters: Westpac is now forecasting the Reserve Bank of Australia will raise interest rates at its meeting next week, after Australia's CPI (inflation) data came in hotter than expected. That would mean higher mortgage repayments for millions of Australians. The Aussie dollar ticked up on the news as traders priced in the possibility of a hike. If confirmed, this would be a significant squeeze on household budgets heading into the holiday season.

stories.title: Albanese calls RBA rate hikes a 'blunt instrument', distances Labor from central bank
stories.why_it_matters: Prime Minister Albanese publicly called interest rate hikes a 'blunt instrument', making clear Labor is uncomfortable with the RBA's approach even as the central bank prepares to potentially raise rates again. This is an unusually direct public comment for a PM about an independent central bank — it signals political tension between the government and the RBA heading into a rate decision week. Albanese appears to be getting ahead of the political fallout if a hike hurts households.

stories.title: Ex-Treasury boss tells Chalmers to slash public service to reach budget surplus
stories.why_it_matters: A former Treasury secretary has publicly urged Treasurer Jim Chalmers to cut the size of the public service to get the federal budget back into surplus. With the government facing spending pressures and inflation still elevated, the advice adds to the political pressure on Labor to tighten fiscal policy. Chalmers has been resisting calls for austerity, arguing targeted spending is needed to ease cost-of-living pressures.

stories.title: Victoria's budget blowout: $7 billion worse than expected, auditor slams repair plan
stories.why_it_matters: Victoria's state budget is $7 billion worse than forecast, and the state's auditor-general has slammed the Andrews-era government's budget repair strategy as inadequate. The blowout raises serious questions about Victoria's ability to fund essential services and manage its debt load. For Victorians, it could mean cuts to services or higher state taxes down the track.

stories.title: Data centre investment at risk as regulatory confusion grows, operators warn
stories.why_it_matters: Data centre operators are warning that unclear government rules around planning, energy, and zoning are putting billions of dollars of investment in Australia at risk. As AI drives huge demand for data centres globally, Australia risks missing out on a wave of tech infrastructure spending if the regulatory environment doesn't improve. This matters for jobs, electricity demand, and Australia's position as a regional tech hub.

ai.summary: The big four AI labs agreed to let websites opt out of AI training. US midterm politics is bleeding into AI safety debates. Healthcare AI regulation is struggling to keep pace with fast-moving products.

stories.title: Anthropic, Google, Microsoft and OpenAI agree websites can opt out of AI training
stories.why_it_matters: The four biggest AI companies — Anthropic (maker of Claude), Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI — have agreed to honour a standard that lets website owners signal they don't want their content used to train AI models. In plain terms: if a website puts up a 'no AI training' flag, these companies will respect it. It's a voluntary agreement rather than law, but it's significant because it's the first time all four major labs have aligned on a common opt-out standard. Content creators and publishers have been pushing for exactly this.

stories.title: AI safety becomes a political football as US midterms approach
stories.why_it_matters: With the US midterms approaching, AI safety regulation has become a genuinely political issue — with some candidates backing tighter controls on frontier AI labs, and others arguing regulation would stifle American competitiveness against China. The debate matters because whatever the US decides will shape global AI regulation, including in Australia. Tech companies like Google and Microsoft are lobbying hard on both sides.

stories.title: FDA and Medicare scrambling to avoid AI regulatory logjam in healthcare
stories.why_it_matters: US health regulators (the FDA and Medicare/Medicaid) are scrambling to create rules for AI tools being used in hospitals and clinics, as more US states start running AI pilots in clinical settings. The problem: AI models get updated constantly, so a product approved today may be quite different six months from now. Regulators are trying to figure out how to handle AI that changes itself. Australia's TGA will face the same challenge — this is a global problem with no clean answer yet.

stories.title: Japan's surge in cyberattacks sparks push for tighter AI and data security rules
stories.why_it_matters: Japan has seen a major spike in sophisticated cyberattacks, many leveraging AI tools, and it's now pushing for tighter national AI and data security regulations. This follows a pattern where countries that experience high-profile AI-enabled cyber incidents end up driving global regulatory conversations. For Australian businesses, it's a reminder that AI governance isn't just about ethics — it's increasingly a national security issue.

sport.summary: It's Rugby League World Cup time — England is in serious trouble after a stunning loss to Papua New Guinea, the NRL draw for next season is taking shape, and AFL is wrapping up with Geelong locking in a top-two finish and Carlton landing a big coaching coup.

stories.title: England stunned by Papua New Guinea, World Cup campaign on the brink
stories.why_it_matters: England's Rugby League World Cup campaign is hanging by a thread after being beaten by the Papua New Guinea Kumuls (the 'Ku-mools') in a gritty upset. England reportedly needed a 'miracle' after the loss, with the headline 'We're going home' capturing the mood. PNG's performance was a massive statement — the Kumuls have been one of the tournament's stories so far, and England's path to the semi-finals is now incredibly narrow.

stories.title: RLWC semi-final race heats up — every team's path mapped out
stories.why_it_matters: With pool play moving through Round 1, NRL.com has mapped out every nation's path to the semi-finals. After England's shock loss and PNG's big win, the semi-final picture is already shifting. Australia and New Zealand are expected to be the dominant forces, but the tournament has already thrown up surprises.

stories.title: NRL 2027 draw whispers: Bruno blocks Broncos, Bears return date revealed
stories.why_it_matters: Whispers about the 2027 NRL draw are circulating — including that Wayne Bennett's club is allegedly 'blocking' the Broncos from a particular fixture, and the return of the South Sydney Bears to a specific venue has been locked in. Still early days, but NRL draw leaks always get plenty of traction among fans planning their season.

stories.title: Roosters win NRL Grand Final 19-18 over Knights in a thriller
stories.why_it_matters: The 2026 NRL Grand Final was decided by just one point — the Sydney Roosters defeated the Newcastle Knights 19-18 at Accor Stadium on Sunday 4 October. It was a tight, tense final befitting the occasion. The Roosters claimed the premiership in dramatic fashion.

stories.title: Carlton lands premiership-winning coach Chris Fagan in AFL coaching coup
stories.why_it_matters: Carlton has pulled off a major AFL coaching coup, locking in Chris Fagan as their new head coach. Fagan, who led Brisbane to the 2023 AFL premiership, said the role gives him 'genuine purpose' and chose Carlton over other offers. It's a significant signing for a club that has been trying to return to finals contention — Fagan has a proven track record of building winning cultures.
